chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Bakr, do you know how many prayers are performed for the deceased?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Five takbirs. Do you know from where the five takbirs were derived?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'The five takbirs were derived from the five salats; from each prayer, one takbir.'
ai.seo_question: What is the number of takbirs in the Shia funeral prayer and what is its scriptural derivation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the five takbirs of the funeral prayer by linking them to the five daily prayers, assigning one takbir to each. This derivation highlights the structural continuity between the ritual of prayer for the living and that for the deceased, a view supported by many Shia jurists who emphasize this numerical symmetry as a sign of divine order in worship.
